history.dynasty: Chalukya (Karnadeva); later Shilahara, Yadava, Maratha additions
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 619 (same Mahalaxmi/Ambabai temple of Kolhapur). Built by Chalukya king Karnadeva in 634 CE in Hemadpanti style, the temple is one of the three-and-a-half Shakti peethas and a cornerstone of the Tirumala-Kolhapur-Padmavathi pilgrimage circuit. Legend says Ambabai killed the demon Kolhasur, giving Kolhapur its name. Twice a year (around 21 March and 21 September) the setting sun shines through a western window directly onto the idol's face (Kirnotsav). The 3-ft black-stone idol (~40 kg) stands on a platform with a lion behind and Shri Yantra carved on a wall. The idol was hidden during Adil Shahi/Mughal attacks and reinstalled in the temple in 1712. Note: scholar Paul Dundas cites a theory that the shrine was originally a Jain temple of Chandraprabha, later converted - contested, treat with caution. Exact timeline beyond the 7th-century foundation is debated across sources.

name: Mahalaxmi Temple (Ambabai Temple)
town_description: Kolhapur is a major city in southwest Maharashtra on the Panchganga river, former capital of the Kolhapur Maratha state and now district headquarters. It is one of Maharashtra's leading pilgrimage centres (Mahalakshmi, Jyotiba, Temblai) and famous for kushti wrestling, Kolhapuri chappals and its historic Bhavani Mandap complex.

travel.road: On NH-48 corridor; temple at Bhavani Mandap, Mahadwar Road in the city centre
